title: Genetic landscape of Autism Spectrum Disorder with Macrocephaly and functional insights from KMT2E variants
description: The heterogeneity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) complicates etiological research. Head circumference, as a direct clinical indicator of brain development, aids in studying the genetic etiology of ASD with macrocephaly (ASD-M). This study aimed to delineate the genetic landscape of ASD-M and generate hypotheses regarding the pathogenic mechanisms of O'Donnell-Luria-Rodan syndrome caused by rare KMT2E mutations. Whole-exome sequencing performed in ASD-M children identified risk genes via OMIM integration. Meanwhile, functional validation of three novel KMT2E mutations was conducted in HEK293T and SH-SY5Y cells. Transcriptomic analyses were performed on two independent sample sets: peripheral blood from a KMT2E mutation carrier versus a neurotypical control, and wild-type versus KMT2E-mutant SH-SY5Y cells.
